answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity something earned through a slow reputation voyage: a new agent must first complete small, verifiable jobs under peer review — bending like a willow under scrutiny rather than snapping into instant trust — before it touches valuable work. Spawning thousands of fakes then costs as much time and compute as building real ones, like crossing a dune one grain at a time, so the attacker's profit collapses while honest agents keep their earned standing.
